text: Feature flags and experiments can be added to an app with a few lines of code using a language-specific SDK
quote: Get GrowthBook feature flags and experiments running in your app in a few lines of code, then pick a language-specific SDK.

text: Rules use targeting conditions evaluated against attributes passed into the SDK, such as user ID, country, plan, or custom properties
quote: Conditions are evaluated against **attributes** you pass into the SDK — like user ID, country, plan type, or any custom property.

text: Flags can be targeted with user attributes, conditions, saved groups, and percentage rollouts
quote: Target feature flags with user attributes, conditions, saved groups, and percentage rollouts.

text: Feature flags can be enabled or disabled independently per environment (dev, staging, production)
quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.

text: Automatically detects stale flags so they can be cleaned up

text: Feature changes can be drafted as revisions, sent for review, have merge conflicts resolved, and require approval before publishing
quote: Draft feature revisions, request review, resolve merge conflicts, and require approval before publishing.

text: Earlier feature revisions can be selected and reverted to

text: Stats engine supports Bayesian and frequentist analysis, CUPED, sequential testing, post-stratification, bandits, and SRM checks
quote: World class experiment stats engine (CUPED, Sequential, Bayesian, Post-Strat, Bandits, SRM checks).

text: Experiment templates pre-fill data source, goal/secondary/guardrail metrics, targeting, and traffic settings
quote: Selecting a Template in the creation modal pre-fills settings like the data source, goal/secondary/guardrail metrics, targeting, and traffic

quote: The primary way to create metrics in GrowthBook is with **Fact Tables** where you write SQL to pull a set of rows and then define multiple metrics on top of those rows.

text: Warehouse-native: queries 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks
quote: Warehouse Native. Query 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks.

text: Experimentation can start without connecting a data warehouse
quote: Skip the setup. Start learning. No need to connect your data warehouse.

text: Can be self-hosted with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end

text: Full REST API for interacting with the application
quote: GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.

text: AI tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Claude can connect to GrowthBook through an official MCP server
quote: Connect AI tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Claude to GrowthBook using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

quote: The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.

text: Risky changes can be held until a person confirms them in GrowthBook
quote: Require confirmation holds risky changes until a person confirms them in GrowthBook.

text: Flags and Visual Editor experiments can be evaluated at the edge on Cloudflare Workers to reduce flicker
quote: Evaluate GrowthBook feature flags and Visual Editor experiments at the edge on Cloudflare Workers to cut flicker before HTML ships.

text: Server-side or hybrid visual experiments can run automatically without redraw flicker
quote: Automatically run server-side or hybrid [Visual Experiments](https://docs.growthbook.io/app/visual) without redraw flicker.

text: AI Visual Editor experiments run on page load without requiring code
quote: AI Visual Editor experiments run when the page loads and do not require code.

quote: Run A/B tests with feature flags, the Visual Editor, URL redirects, or your own assignment, then analyze results in GrowthBook.

text: Experiment rules on a feature randomly assign users to variations based on a hashing attribute
quote: you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.

text: Server-side inline experiments can run directly with the SDK, with no third-party requests
quote: You can also run server-side experiments by using inline experiments directly with our SDK. This requires no 3rd party requests

quote: Analyze A/B test results in GrowthBook: statistical analysis, health checks, custom reports, and how to interpret the data.

text: Experiment results can be fetched through an API endpoint for your own reporting

quote: Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.

quote: const showNewFeature = useFeatureIsOn("new-feature"); const buttonColor = useFeatureValue("button-color", "blue");

text: 24 SDKs including React, Python, Android, and iOS
quote: 24 SDKs including React, Python, Android, and iOS.

text: All SDKs share the same assignment logic, so identical attributes produce the same variation in any SDK
quote: All SDKs use the same assignment logic, so the same attributes always produce the same variation regardless of which SDK you use.

text: React SDK supports ReactJS and React Native, with both client and server components
quote: This SDK supports both ReactJS and ReactNative environments and both client and server components.

text: Android SDK supports Java and Kotlin apps on Android SDK 21 and above
quote: This SDK supports both Java and Kotlin Android apps using Android SDK 21 and above.

text: Swift SDK supports iOS, macOS, tvOS, and other Apple platforms
quote: Install the GrowthBook Swift SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests on iOS, macOS, tvOS, and other Apple platforms.

text: Flutter SDK supports mobile, web, and desktop apps
quote: Install the GrowthBook Flutter SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests in Flutter mobile, web, and desktop apps.

text: An HTML script tag runs flags and Visual Editor experiments on any website or low-code platform
quote: Add a GrowthBook HTML script tag to any website or low-code platform to run feature flags and Visual Editor experiments.

text: SDK test suite provides over 400 language-agnostic unit tests in JSON format
quote: At the end of this guide is an extensive test suite with over 400 language-agnostic unit tests in JSON format.

text: Feature evaluation happens wherever the SDK runs: browser, server, or edge
quote: This evaluation happens wherever the SDK runs—in the browser, on your server, or at the edge.

text: Targeting attribute values stay in local SDK memory and are never sent to GrowthBook
quote: The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.

text: Read-only SDK Connection Endpoint exposes only the flag data SDKs need to assign values
quote: The SDK Connection Endpoint provides readonly access to a subset of your feature flag data, just enough for the GrowthBook SDKs to assign values to users.

text: Streaming pushes feature changes to apps in real time (JavaScript and React only)
quote: **Streaming** - Updates your application in real-time as features are changed or toggled in GrowthBook (JavaScript and React only)

text: Remote evaluation hides feature business logic in insecure environments
quote: **Remote Evaluation** - Hide your features' business logic in insecure environments

text: Offline-first SDK mode works without network connectivity using cached features
quote: **Offline-First**: Works without network connectivity using cached features

text: Switching to or from GrowthBook via OpenFeature only requires changing the provider bootstrap
quote: Switching from or to GrowthBook only requires changing the provider bootstrap, not a single flag call.

quote: automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
